clue.text: Lick the top off? That's disgusting!

indicators.note: taking the top off a word in an across answer means removing its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written, before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from the idea of licking something clean, or licking the froth off.
explanation.walkthrough: LICK loses its L to leave ICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Ick is an informal exclamation of revulsion, so it stands for an outburst of disgust.

clue.text: Religious paintings smuggled by Bolshevik on ship

indicators.note: smuggled goods are concealed inside, so the answer is tucked within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A Bolshevik sneaks religious icons out of Russia aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikons, a variant spelling of icons, are devotional paintings of holy figures in the Orthodox Church.

clue.text: Recording of trashy American boy band is something always left behind

indicators.note: a recording is something listened to, so the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: kitsch means trashy, and NSYNC was a US boy band

explanation.surface: A record by a tacky American boy band is always the one left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'everything but the kitchen sink' means taking absolutely everything except that one thing.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom, the kitchen sink is the single item that is never taken along, so it is always left behind.

clue.text: Choir performing west of Hull, accompanied by first footman?

indicators.note: performing suggests these letters are put through their paces and rearranged
in an across answer, west of means placed to the left, so this piece comes first

parts.note: the letters of choir rearranged
a pod is the hull or shell of peas and beans
first written as 1ST, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A choir sings somewhere west of the city of Hull, joined by an eighteenth-century servant leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the Yorkshire city; it is the pod around peas. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiropodist treats people's feet, so jokingly a footman is a 'man for feet' rather than a liveried servant.

clue.text: Man at the back of Aldi making bread

parts.note: a chap is a man
taken as written

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of the supermarket name

explanation.surface: A man at the rear of an Aldi supermarket is baking bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened bread from South Asia.

clue.text: Clown in Stephen King novel comprehending the origins of depravity in ourselves

indicators.note: comprehending in the sense of including or taking in, so the novel's title surrounds the letters

parts.note: It is Stephen King's horror novel

indicators.note: the origins of words are their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: The clown in King's horror novel brings out the depravity in all of us.
explanation.walkthrough: The clown Pennywise is the monster of It, which is a neat surface trap. IT holds DIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Clown can mean a foolish person, which is what an idiot is.

clue.text: Bed that is put inside once the aim of dog training's achieved

indicators.note: put inside means placed within the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written, to receive the other pieces after its first letter
taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: Once the dog is trained, it goes to its bed when told.
explanation.walkthrough: The two short pieces go in together just after the first letter of the host word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog training is about getting a dog to obey commands, and obedience is that compliance.

clue.text: Notice old bishop beginning to rally

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
in tennis a serve begins each rally

explanation.surface: People notice an elderly bishop starting to recover his health.
explanation.walkthrough: Rally sounds like recovery; it is a tennis exchange, which starts with a serve.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe something is to notice or see it.

clue.text: Cut diamonds — cut diamonds?

parts.note: to dice vegetables is to cut them into cubes
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds, cut away from the verb

explanation.surface: A puzzled repetition asks what the phrase cut diamonds really means.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'Cut diamonds' is wordplay, DICE with its D cut out; the repeated phrase is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is slang for diamonds, particularly polished, cut stones.

clue.text: Pieces of rat's tail quietly consumed by someone struggling

indicators.note: struggling letters are thrashing about out of order
a tail is at the rear, so take the final letter of the animal

parts.note: the final letter of the rodent's name

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed up inside something else

parts.note: the letters of someone rearranged
p for piano, the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Bits of a rat's tail are quietly eaten by someone in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces means musical works, not bits. T then ONE(P)OEMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tone poems are orchestral compositions, and pieces is a common word for musical works.

clue.text: East German is framed by trial and put on the blacklist

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east

indicators.note: something framed is surrounded on every side, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a race such as a time trial is a contest
taken as written, set inside the contest word

explanation.surface: An East German suspect is put on trial and blacklisted, a Cold War show trial.
explanation.walkthrough: A time trial is a race against the clock, which is why trial can mean a contest here.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracise is to exclude someone from society, which is what blacklisting a person does.

clue.text: Small seabird in the back of boat

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tern is a slender gull-like seabird

explanation.surface: A little seabird perches in the rear of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear part of a ship or boat, opposite the bow.

clue.text: After school meal, Ritz crackers becoming mushier

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild and are reordered
after places the rearranged material behind the first short piece in the answer

parts.note: SCH is the standard abbreviation for school
the letters of meal and Ritz mixed together

explanation.surface: After a school dinner, Ritz crackers are served, and the whole occasion gets more sentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: Ritz crackers looks like the biscuit brand; crackers is the signal. Schmaltz is Yiddish for chicken fat, hence sentimental excess.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltzy means excessively sentimental, as is mushy, so the comparatives match.

clue.text: A bit of sauce — just over half a pound?

wordplay.note: fifty-one pence, written LI in Roman numerals and P for pence, a little more than half of a hundred pence

explanation.surface: A cook measures out a little sauce, a shade over eight ounces.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound means money, not weight: a pound is 100 pence, so 51p is just over half.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce and lip are both informal words for cheek or impudence, so a bit of sauce is some lip.

clue.text: Circle around small lakes, heading north, most of them boring

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so this piece goes inside
in a down answer, heading north means going upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: pools are small lakes, and the plural is taken as two of them

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: taken as written, before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone walks round a circuit of little lakes, heading north, finding most of them dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Boring looks like dull; it means drilling into. THE goes inside LOOPLOOP.
explanation.definitionFit: To loop the loop is to fly an aircraft in a complete vertical circle.

clue.text: Dissatisfaction of tiddly nun that is returning drinks

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the abbreviation is read from right to left
something that drinks takes another thing inside itself

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is

indicators.note: tiddly means slightly drunk, so the word staggers into a new order

parts.note: the letters of nun shuffled

explanation.surface: A slightly drunk nun knocks back drinks out of sheer discontent.
explanation.walkthrough: IE reversed is EI, which takes in NNU: E(NNU)I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is weary boredom and listlessness, a kind of dissatisfaction with life.

clue.text: Dress up those people in East London like Big Ben?

parts.note: 'em, the dropped-h form of them in Cockney speech
Big Ben is the great bell of the Westminster clock tower, so bell plus -ish, like

explanation.surface: Eastenders dress up in a way resembling a famous London landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech of East London drops sounds, so them becomes 'em.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish is to decorate or adorn, which is to dress something up.

clue.text: Long flag extracted from both ends of blue post

parts.note: the first and last letters of blue, read literally as 'B and E', word and included
a post is a job or role

explanation.surface: A long blue flag is pulled out from both ends of a flagpole.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to read the phrase as a spoken instruction rather than a selection: the connecting word survives into the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A banderole is a long narrow streamer or pennant flown from a mast or lance.

clue.text: Pretty black fauteuil is broken

indicators.note: something broken comes apart and its parts end up out of place

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
the letters of this armchair word rearranged

explanation.surface: A pretty black armchair has broken.
explanation.walkthrough: A fauteuil is a French upholstered armchair.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty and beautiful both describe something attractive to look at.

clue.text: Badminton lessons initially at home — then daughters had singles match

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the two words

parts.note: the first letters of these two words
someone at home is in
D is daughter, doubled for the plural
to have a meal is to eat it, so had can mean ate

explanation.surface: Badminton coaching at home, then the daughters play a singles game.
explanation.walkthrough: Singles match looks like sport, extending the badminton picture; it is a meeting arranged for two unattached people.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind date is a romantic meeting set up between two single people who have never met.

clue.text: How to get 7 from office and make delivery

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an instruction to remove three letters from that word, leaving the answer to 7 Down
second meaning: to leave goods or a passenger at a destination

explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 7 Down is ICE, which is what office becomes once its first three letters are taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a literal instruction to omit a chunk and the everyday verb for delivering a parcel or passenger.

clue.text: Quotes from scenes on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so go by sound alone

parts.note: scenes are sites or locations, and that word is said the same as the answer

explanation.surface: A broadcaster quotes passages from scenes of a radio play.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite a source is to quote or refer to it, so cites works as the verb quotes.

clue.text: Ears? Ears are going to become noteworthy features of this grid

parts.note: ears of grain on a stalk are corn

indicators.note: going means departing, so the unit named are leaves the word

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for are, the metric unit of area

explanation.surface: A puzzled solver is told that ears will be the notable features of the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The four corner answers each pair with corner: CORNER KICK, CORNERSTONE, CORNER SHOP and POETS' CORNER.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle's theme sits in its four corners, so the corners are this grid's notable features.

clue.text: Remove earth from vegetable and make bread in Albania

indicators.note: remove instructs us to take a letter out of the following word

parts.note: a leek is an onion-family vegetable
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A cook in Albania cleans the soil off a leek and bakes bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money; LEEK minus one E.
explanation.definitionFit: The lek is the currency of Albania, and bread is slang for money.

clue.text: Fine time carousing before street party

indicators.note: carousing is drunken revelry, so the next word reels about into a new order

parts.note: OK means fine or acceptable
T is the abbreviation for time
the letters of before jumbled
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: People have a great time drinking before a street party.
explanation.walkthrough: Before looks like a positional word; it is the fodder for carousing.
explanation.definitionFit: Oktoberfest is Munich's annual beer festival, a huge party.

clue.text: Get up and get undressed to get lighter

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to grab something is to get hold of it

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer layers, leaving only the middle

parts.note: the middle letter once the outer two are removed

explanation.surface: Someone gets out of bed and strips off to feel lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: A lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships, not a cigarette lighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a type of flat boat used to ferry cargo, and a barge is one such vessel.

clue.text: Some detest a steak's flavour

indicators.note: some means part of, so the answer is a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through to the start of the third

explanation.surface: Some people hate the flavour of steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste and flavour are synonyms for the quality of food sensed in the mouth.

clue.text: State in India harboured revolutionary circle

parts.note: India is the NATO alphabet word for I

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to harbour a feeling is to have it, so harboured means had
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: An Indian state sheltered a revolutionary group.
explanation.walkthrough: India looks like the country; it is the radio code for I, and the state is in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the north-west.

clue.text: Cleopatra's end? Cleopatra's heart stopped by this serpentine character

indicators.note: a gap stopped by something is plugged with it, so a letter sits between the other two
the end of a name is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the queen's name
S is the snake-shaped letter

indicators.note: 'heart' keeps only the middle letter of 'Cleopatra'

parts.note: the middle letter of the nine-letter name

explanation.surface: The queen's death came from a snake, the serpent at the heart of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra is said to have died from the bite of a snake. A and P hold S between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An asp, the Egyptian cobra, is traditionally held to have killed Cleopatra, so it was her end.

clue.text: After travelling, Beowulf's protecting Hrothgar's backside to get fancy ornaments

indicators.note: after travelling the letters have moved about and arrive in a new order
protecting means surrounding something to shield it

parts.note: the letters of Beowulfs rearranged, about to hold a single letter

indicators.note: a backside is the rear, so take the final letter of the name

parts.note: the last letter of the king's name

explanation.surface: In the epic, travelling hero Beowulf guards the rear of King Hrothgar's hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Hrothgar is the Danish king whom Beowulf aids in the Old English poem. FU(R)BELOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Furbelows are showy frills and flounces on clothing, so fancy ornaments.

clue.text: Optimism of lush seen dancing around Penny

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and take up new positions
around means surrounding the single letter that follows

parts.note: these three words' letters rearranged
P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A drunk is spotted dancing round someone called Penny, full of optimism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like a link word but its O and F are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopefulness is the state of being hopeful, a synonym for optimism.

clue.text: Writer's verse left unfinished

indicators.note: left unfinished means the final letter is missing

parts.note: a poem is a piece of verse

explanation.surface: An author's poem has been abandoned half-written.
explanation.walkthrough: POEM loses its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was an American author of stories and poems.
